data.name: Ekagrah
data.long_meaning: The name Ekagrah is derived from the Sanskrit word 'eka' meaning one and 'agrah' meaning point or focus. It represents a person with a single-minded focus or intense concentration. In Hindu mythology, Ekagrah is also associated with Lord Shiva, who is known for his unwavering focus and intense devotion.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Ekagrah is the name of a powerful demon who was vanquished by Lord Shiva. Ekagrah was born from the mind of the demon Tripura, and was characterized by his single-minded focus and determination to destroy Lord Shiva. He is often depicted as having only one eye, representing his unwavering focus on his goal.

Ekagrah is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of a powerful yogi who attained the ability to see the past, present, and future. He was able to do this through intense meditation and focus, symbolized by the name Ekagrah (one-pointed).
